newsitem.title: BELGIUM: New Belgian airline to fly to US from March 97.
newsitem.headline: New Belgian airline to fly to US from March 97.

text.p: A new Belgian airline City Bird, owned by Belgian hotel group City Hotels, will begin flying from Brussels to the U.S. on 27 March next year.
City Hotels formed EBA Airlines in 1991 and sold its share in the company to Richard Branson's Virgin Group last May.
"Following the success of EBA, we have decided to use our air transport experience to create a new airline specialised in long haul flights from Brussels," City Hotels said in a statement Thursday.
City Hotels holds 62.5 percent of City Bird, which will fly 371-seat MD-11 aircraft to New York, Miami, Orlando, Los Angeles and San Francisco.
The venture is in association with Belgian tour operator NUR Touristic group, which owns Neckerman, Sunsnacks, Pegase and AllAir.
"Most Belgian long haul passengers presently have no option but to travel via foreign airports, and with foreign airlines," City Hotels said.
The company said the success of EBA Express showed that the development of a cheap and original product meets market demand and can stimulate passenger numbers.
Prices will be in line with EBA policy, which City Hotels described as "constantly low prices and no restrictions".
NUR Touristic plans to charter City Bird aircraft for holiday destinations, while City Bird will offer scheduled flights to the U.S.
